# Black Powder Composition

Black powder (also known as gunpowder) is a mixture of three components:

| Component | Typical Proportion |
|---|---|
| **Potassium nitrate** (saltpeter/KNO₃) | ~75% |
| **Charcoal** (carbon) | ~15% |
| **Sulfur** | ~10% |

## Role of Each Component

- **Potassium nitrate** – Acts as the **oxidizer**, providing oxygen for the combustion reaction
- **Charcoal** – Serves as the primary **fuel**
- **Sulfur** – Acts as a secondary fuel and **lowers the ignition temperature**, making the mixture easier to ignite

## Key Points

- The exact ratios have varied throughout history and by application
- The fineness of the grind and how well the components are incorporated affect performance
- It was historically used in firearms, mining, fireworks, and demolition
- It has largely been replaced by smokeless powder in modern firearms and by other explosives in industrial applications

Black powder was one of the most significant inventions in history, originating in **China** around the 9th century and later spreading to Europe and the rest of the world.
